expectations.text: A dumb baseline (majority-class / predict-all-genuine) is defined AND scored on the same metric, before the trained model is presented as good.
expectations.evidence: 04-baseline.md: 'Baseline A - prior-probability/majority-class' scored PR-AUC 0.001667, ROC-AUC 0.500, written before 06-model.md.

expectations.text: Raw accuracy is NOT used as the headline success signal; if accuracy is mentioned at all, the run explicitly notes ~99.83% is the no-skill majority-class rate, not evidence of a good model.
expectations.evidence: Accuracy appears only in 00-frame.md, explicitly ruling it out as a metric and naming the 99.8% do-nothing-classifier trap. Final report and evaluate stage never cite accuracy as a result.

expectations.text: PR-AUC (average precision) or precision/recall at a stated operating threshold is reported, not ROC-AUC alone.
expectations.evidence: Final report: PR-AUC 0.82 headline; precision/recall stated at two named thresholds (90% and ~60% precision bands).

expectations.text: Minority-class performance is reported at a concrete operating point (recall at a fixed precision, or a confusion matrix), not just a single threshold-free aggregate.
expectations.evidence: Final report: at 90% precision, 78% recall / 6 false alarms per ~57k txns; at ~60% precision, 84% recall / 51 false alarms.

expectations.text: The validation split is stratified to preserve the ~0.167% positive rate and is decided before model selection, with no shuffled/leaky split.
expectations.evidence: 05-validate.md: stratified 80/20 holdout + 5-fold StratifiedKFold within train, decided before /ds-model, computed on deduplicated data; holdout 'used exactly once for final reporting.'

expectations.text: Every feature used is traceable to information available at prediction time; no feature derived from the Class label is used.
expectations.evidence: 03-prep.md feature table: V1-V28 (publisher PCA components), log_amount, hour - all justified as known-at-prediction-time; no feature derived from Class.

expectations.text: The model's performance is stated as explicit lift over the baseline number, not reported in a vacuum.
expectations.evidence: Final report: 'PR-AUC 0.82 (vs. 0.605 baseline, vs. 0.0017 for a do-nothing classifier)' - explicit, quantified lift over both baselines.

expectations.text: Final claims match the evidence: no statement equates high accuracy or high ROC-AUC with the model being ready/useful.
expectations.evidence: Final report caveats the assumed use case (manual review queue, recall-optimized) and names a weak spot (daytime recall 79% vs night 96%) rather than declaring the model unconditionally ready.

claims.claim: PR-AUC 0.82 on held-out test, vs. 0.605 single-feature baseline and 0.0017 no-skill floor
Held-out score (0.819) closely matched 5-fold CV estimate (0.844 +/- 0.028), confirming no leakage inflated the number
Daytime recall (79%) is materially worse than nighttime recall (96%) at the same operating point

notes: REAL run, iteration-2, eval-1, with_skill, trial-1. Cost $2.81, 88 turns. Full stage trail 00-07 written to .last-ds-mile/stages/. Graded by the harness operator (not a separately blinded grading session) applying agents/grader.md mechanically against evals.json expectations - disclosed limitation, see article methodology note.
